title: Diagonalizable group over an arbitrary scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $M$ an additive abelian group. Define the $S$-group scheme $D_S(M)$ by base change [def-pc-base-change] of $D_{\mathbf Z}(M)=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[M]$ with its Hopf operations [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] along the unique morphism $S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Equivalently it is obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$, with coproduct $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$, counit $e_m\mapsto1$ and antipode $e_m\mapsto e_{-m}$. No finite-generation, nonempty-base or field hypothesis is required.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Appendix B.1, printed p.280, diagonalizable group D_S(M); integral model and affine group-algebra base-change construction.
